title: Bits to Flip Between Two Numbers
statement:
You get two non-negative integers start and goal. In one move you pick any single bit of start's binary form and flip it, from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0. You may flip bits above the highest set bit too; those are leading zeros.

Return the fewest moves needed to turn start into goal.

examples.why: 1010 and 0111 differ in three positions: bits 0, 2 and 3.
The numbers are 9 apart, but in binary 1101 and 0100 differ in only two positions. Moves count bits, not distance.
Every set bit of the goal has to be turned on, and a billion has 13 of them.

hints: Each bit position can be handled on its own. When does a position need a flip?
A position needs a flip exactly when the two numbers have different bits there. Which operator marks those positions with a 1?
XOR the numbers, then count the 1 bits in the result, for example by clearing the lowest set bit with v & (v − 1) until it reaches 0.

explain.intuition:
Flipping one bit never affects any other bit, so the positions are independent. A position must be flipped once if start and goal disagree there, and never if they agree. So the answer is the number of positions where they disagree.

XOR is exactly "do these bits disagree?": start ^ goal has a 1 wherever they differ. Counting the 1s in it (the popcount) is the answer. The trick v &= v − 1 clears the lowest set bit, so the loop runs once per set bit rather than once per position.
steps: While v is not 0: do v &= v − 1 and add 1 to count.
pitfalls: Using the numeric difference |start − goal|. 13 and 4 are 9 apart, but only 2 bits differ.
Comparing only up to the length of the shorter binary string, which misses bits where one number has leading zeros.
Counting set bits of start and goal separately and subtracting. 1 and 2 both have one set bit, but they need 2 flips.

solutions.title: Compare bit by bit
solutions.idea: Shift both numbers right together and count positions where the lowest bits differ.

solutions.title: XOR and clear lowest set bit
solutions.idea: XOR marks the differing positions; clearing one set bit per step counts them.

followups: Given an array of numbers, find the total number of differing bits over all pairs. Can you avoid looking at each pair?
Why does v & (v − 1) clear exactly the lowest set bit?
lcTitle: Minimum Bit Flips to Convert Number
